:::{#exm-exchangeability-strata}
#### A population where exchangeability holds only within strata

Consider a large population of 1000 patients,
with a binary covariate $L$ (disease severity: $L = 1$ for severe)
and treatment $A$.
Severe patients are more likely to be treated,
and both potential outcomes are higher for severe patients
(treating proportions as probabilities):

| $L$ | patients | $\Pf{A = 1 \mid L}$ | treated | untreated | $\E{Y(1) \mid L}$ | $\E{Y(0) \mid L}$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 0 | 600 | 0.2 | 120 | 480 | 10 | 8 |
| 1 | 400 | 0.7 | 280 | 120 | 20 | 18 |

Within each severity stratum,
suppose treatment was assigned as if at random,
so that $A \ind (Y(0), Y(1)) \mid L$:
conditional exchangeability (@def-exchangeability) holds with $\vec{L} = L$.

Unconditional exchangeability (@def-unconditional-exchangeability) fails, though.
Averaging $Y(0)$ over the strata in proportion to each treatment group's members:

$$
\ba
\E{Y(0) \mid A = 1}
&= \frac{120 \cdot 8 + 280 \cdot 18}{400}
&& \text{(average over the 400 treated)} \\
&= \frac{960 + 5040}{400}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= 15
&& \text{(add and divide)} \\
\E{Y(0) \mid A = 0}
&= \frac{480 \cdot 8 + 120 \cdot 18}{600}
&& \text{(average over the 600 untreated)} \\
&= \frac{3840 + 2160}{600}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= 10
&& \text{(add and divide)}
\ea
$$

The treated group would have had a higher mean outcome even without treatment,
because it contains more severe patients,
so $A$ is not independent of $Y(0)$.

:::
